newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle first-quarter sales rise 18.7 percent.
newsitem.headline: Nestle first-quarter sales rise 18.7 percent.

text.p: Swiss food and beverage group Nestle SA said Tuesday group sales rose 18.7 percent in the first quarter to 16.1 billion Swiss francs ($11 billion) and it expected good growth in sales and profits in the current year.
"The preliminary April figures confirm this trend," Nestle said in a statement released at its annual news conference.
Most of the sales increase, however, came from favourable exchange rates and the growth rate is likely to ease during the second half of the year, Nestle added.
In the first quarter sales volume grew 2.2 percent.
The stock market reacted with disappointment to Nestle's results, pushing down the stock by almost one percent to 1,820 francs shortly after the results were announced.
The market had generally been looking for a rise in first-quarter sales of around 20 percent compared with the reported 18.7 percent, dealers said.
In 1996 Nestle's sales grew 7.1 percent to 60.49 billion francs ($41.4 billion) and net profit rose 16.6 percent to 3.40 billion francs ($2.33 billion).
